# OpenAI Responses protocol examples

Retrieved **2026-10-25**. `examples.json` is handwritten from the official schemas and guides
below. It is not a recording, copied documentation example, SDK output, live API test, or proof
that a particular account/model supports these features. No credentials or upstream source code
were used. The model, item/response/call/file IDs, encrypted reasoning, prose, timestamps and
usage counts are synthetic. The embedded image is an independently constructed one-pixel PNG.
The encrypted string is deliberately not replayable; file IDs do not identify uploaded files.

The outer `requests`, `responses`, `streams`, and sample `id` fields are fixture metadata.
Request `body` values model `POST /v1/responses`; response `body` values model Response objects.
Each stream entry records an SSE event name and its parsed JSON `data`, without HTTP headers
or SSE framing. These are minimal illustrative sequences, not an exhaustive lifecycle trace
for every model. They preserve the documented distinction between `output_index`,
`content_index`/`summary_index`, item `id`, and function `call_id`.

## Examples

| Sample ID | Coverage |
|---|---|
| `responses-multimodal-input` | User text, inline image with detail, and uploaded-file reference |
| `responses-tool-reasoning-replay` | Full reasoning item, assistant commentary phase, two distinct calls, string result, text/image/file result array |
| `responses-refusal-replay` | Refusal preserved as an assistant refusal part in later input |
| `responses-tool-calls` | Reasoning and commentary followed by two client-executed function calls |
| `responses-annotated-final` | Final-answer phase and a URL annotation with offsets |
| `responses-refusal` | Completed response containing a refusal; status alone is insufficient |
| `responses-max-tokens`, `responses-content-filter`, `responses-max-messages`, `responses-steered` | Four distinct documented incomplete reasons |
| `responses-cancelled`, `responses-failed` | Cancellation versus generation failure; usage may be absent/null |
| `responses-hosted-image` | Image generated by a hosted tool, rather than an assistant image content part |
| `responses-tool-success-stream` | Reasoning summary, text, and interleaved function argument deltas; reverse-order call completion |
| `responses-refusal-stream`, `responses-incomplete-stream` | Refusal lifecycle versus token-limit incomplete lifecycle |
| `responses-error-stream`, `responses-failed-stream` | Top-level `error` event versus `response.failed` containing `response.error` |

## Mapping notes for the current canonical contracts

These are research conclusions and proposed adapter behavior, not implemented conversions.
“Reverse” for events means reconstructing a wire trace; normal API requests replay completed
items, not delta events. A canonical flat index is adapter-assigned: keep a stable lookup from
wire item ID plus content/summary position. Do not reuse `output_index` for every nested part,
and do not renumber a parallel call when a different call completes first. [Streaming reference][stream]

| Canonical part | Canonical → Responses | Responses → canonical / missing information |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | User/system text becomes `input_text`; previous assistant text can be `output_text` inside an assistant message. | Text value survives. `annotations`, `logprobs`, message ID/status/phase and original grouping have no typed fields. |
| `image` | Resolve the blob to an `input_image` data URL, including MIME type; a tool result can also contain `input_image`. | Import bytes into blob storage. A URL/file ID requires resolution; image detail, original locator and cache marker are lost. Hosted image output also needs tool provenance preserved. |
| `reasoning` | Replay the original full reasoning item from provider-bound `opaque` to its original provider/model. A summary alone cannot recreate encrypted content. | Keep the entire completed item in `opaque`, including ID, summary array, encrypted content, optional reasoning text and status. Flattened `summary` is only a display projection. |
| `tool_call` | `providerCallId` supplies `call_id`; `name` and untouched `rawArguments` supply function fields. | Allocate local `callId`; preserve wire `call_id` as `providerCallId`. The separate item `id`, namespace/caller/async metadata and status are gaps. |
| `tool_result` | Resolve local `callId` through the original call to `call_id`; emit `function_call_output.output` as text or text/image array. | Result text/images can be imported, but files cannot. Wire item `status` describes generation lifecycle, not the canonical succeeded/failed/denied/cancelled/unknown effect outcome; explicit result text is needed to communicate those outcomes. |

Images, files and result arrays follow the [vision][vision], [file][files] and
[function calling][functions] guides. Blob resolution is adapter I/O, not a new field in this
research change. Ordinary assistant output message content lists text/refusal, not `input_image`.

| Canonical stream event | Responses → canonical | Canonical → wire limitation |
|---|---|---|
| `text_delta` | `response.output_text.delta.delta` with stable nested-part mapping | Cannot recover item ID, output/content positions or logprobs from the flat index alone. |
| `reasoning_delta` | Summary-text deltas project to visible reasoning; distinguish `response.reasoning_text.delta` if supported. | No discriminator for summary versus reasoning text, and no summary index; do not claim exact reconstruction. |
| `tool_call_delta` | Accumulate `response.function_call_arguments.delta.delta` by call item ID. | Requires the item/call identity captured at item creation, absent from this event. |
| `part_completed` | Final text/refusal content can be projected at content completion; full reasoning and call items settle at `response.output_item.done`. | Reconstructing content/item boundaries and metadata requires a retained envelope. Never finalize reasoning from the initial item-added payload. |
| `completed` | Classify `response.completed` by its actual output; token-limit `response.incomplete` can settle with `max_tokens`. | No full Response envelope or original incomplete reason can be reconstructed from stop reason and usage alone. |
| `error` | Map SSE `error`, `response.failed`, HTTP/transport failures, cancellation or unexpected EOF; compute `partialOutput` from completed canonical parts. | Canonical kind/message lose wire error code, parameter, response metadata and exact HTTP/stream source. Retry timing comes from transport evidence, not an invented JSON field. |

Emit only one canonical terminal event; a stream ending without a provider terminal is not
successful. Hosted tools, audio, annotations and other item events must not silently become
ordinary function deltas or vanish. No error-kind lookup for every provider code is established
by these examples. [Streaming reference][stream]

| Canonical stop reason | Responses → canonical | Canonical → Responses |
|---|---|---|
| `end_turn` | Completed response without pending client function calls or a refusal | Can describe a completed result, but does not recover its message phase or content. |
| `tool_use` | Completed response with client function calls awaiting local results | Reconstruct function items, not a wire `finish_reason`; hosted tool activity does not imply local execution. |
| `max_tokens` | Incomplete with reason `max_output_tokens` | Recovers that reason only; output/status/usage still need preservation. |
| `refusal` | A refusal content part; content-filter truncation is a separate signal | Cannot recreate refusal text/boundaries or distinguish `content_filter` from a refusal from this enum alone. |
| `interrupted` | Runtime persistence after cancellation, broken transport or other interruption | No equivalent reusable response item. Do not emit successful canonical completion for an aborted request. |

`max_messages`, `steered`, missing/unknown incomplete reasons, mixed refusal/tool output and
nonterminal queued/in-progress responses need explicit adapter policy; none is safely equivalent
to ordinary completion. `steered` can precede an automatically created successor on WebSocket,
which does not fit “exactly one request” without a defined boundary. [Response schema][create]

| Canonical usage | Responses → canonical | Canonical → Responses |
|---|---|---|
| `inputTokens` | `usage.input_tokens` | Same count if known |
| `outputTokens` | `usage.output_tokens` | Same total; reasoning and invisible formatting tokens are included, not added again |
| `cacheReadTokens` | `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` | Same cache-read breakdown if known |
| `cacheWriteTokens` | `usage.input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` | Same cache-write breakdown if known |

The current schema includes cache writes. These detail counters break down input usage; do not
add them to `input_tokens` again. `output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` and provider
`total_tokens` have no canonical fields. `total_tokens` is derivable from known input/output
totals; the reasoning breakdown is not. Null/absent usage cannot truthfully become mandatory
zero counts. Cache controls such as `prompt_cache_breakpoint` and request cache options are also
not represented by the current rendered request. [Caching][cache], [reasoning guide][reasoning]

## Replay and feature gaps

The current reasoning guide says stateless responses include encrypted reasoning by default;
the legacy `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` in the replay sample remains accepted.
Use the finalized item from `response.output_item.done`, not possibly partial ciphertext from
`response.output_item.added`. Preserve assistant `phase` (`commentary` or `final_answer`) as well
as reasoning data. Phase belongs to assistant messages, not user messages or reasoning items.
An opaque reasoning item alone cannot preserve a neighboring assistant message's phase.
[Reasoning guide][reasoning]

The canonical union lacks file, audio, refusal and annotation variants. The current stream
reference defines audio byte/transcript events, while the inspected create input union specifies
text/image/file content and supplies no typed `input_audio` alternative. This fixture therefore
does not invent one or assert model-level audio support. Consult the [audio guide][audio] and
model capability documentation before any implementation.

Hosted search, code interpreter, image generation, MCP, computer actions, compaction and custom
tool items carry distinct schemas and authority boundaries. An image's bytes can fit `ImagePart`,
but that does not retain its hosted-call identity or other metadata. Do not turn already-executed
hosted tool items into local executable `ToolCallPart`s. Arbitrary custom-tool text is not JSON
function arguments. Provider-owned compaction is also not equivalent to local text compaction.
These require a retained provider item envelope or explicit unsupported handling, subject to D2;
this fixture does not change the persisted format. [Response schema][create]
